identification: Vintage (probably 1920s-1940s) yellow gold half-hoop ring with white metal (platinum or white gold) square illusion settings holding three small old-cut diamonds in a row, and small stones on the shoulders. Shank carries a worn rectangular cartouche stamp plus a smaller mark; in the enlarged photo I could not read it, so 18ct is claimed by the lot title but not confirmed. Colour is a warm yellow-red, consistent with 18ct. 2.7g gross including stones, size O.

searches_tried: comps.py (work and pipeline) for '18ct diamond ring', '18ct platinum diamond ring', 'three stone diamond ring'. Gowans 18ct gold/diamond rings 2-3g sell about $220-$470 hammer in the last year, with the gold and platinum diamond type $290-$505 (one bent at $130). Armitage Launceston similar 18ct diamond rings $130-$680. Melt of about 2g of 18ct gold is only roughly $150-$200 at current prices (not looked up, gold price not checked), so most of the price is stones and period appeal. No web searches or eBay sold prices done; this is a generic category with plentiful local comps. eBay sold would add little.

viewing_check: Read the shank stamp under a loupe (18CT, PLAT, or a UK assay mark) and confirm the metal. Check that all three centre stones and the shoulder stones are present and not chipped, look at stone size and colour, and check the shank for thinness or past repair at the back.
